parents.title: Critical-line zero counting is reduced to zeros of a mollified differential combination

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The reduction replaces direct critical-line zero counting by a chain of representations: parity of completed-zeta derivatives makes zeros of the completed function on the line equivalent, under the stated construction, to zeros of Re eta; argument variation detects such real-part zeros; an approximation V and mollifier B then enlarge the count to zeros of VB; and Littlewood's lemma bounds that count through a shifted mollified mean square. The bookkeeping is not interchangeable: zeros on the critical line carry half weight in the intermediate V and VB counts, whereas the Littlewood count is stated without that convention. Treating the shift and mollifier length as optimization parameters is an inference, not part of the recovered formulas.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Organizes the proof as a typed reduction and uses the differing multiplicity conventions to show what each bridge gains: tractability is purchased by moving from a boundary real-part zero count to a two-dimensional auxiliary zero count and finally an integral norm.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the architecture and counting conventions are prose-visible and support a concrete conceptual reduction without repairing damaged formulas.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span states the real/pure-imaginary parity, the equivalence between a completed-zeta zero and Re eta=0 on the line, the argument-variation zero count, the approximation by V, the mollifier B with a free shift and eventual length choice, the inequality from the V count to the VB count, and the Littlewood mean-square reduction. It explicitly records half-weight conventions and a separate no-half-weight convention.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Only the parameter-control reading is inferential. parents.title: A two-shift local mean proposition generates the required differentiated global mean

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Instead of differentiating a zeta mean at the outset, the proof establishes a proposition for an analytic two-shift family g and then applies Cauchy's integral formula together with the Q differential operation to recover the mean needed for Theorem 2. The shifts therefore function, inferentially, as derivative-generating variables. This representation gains reuse across the differentiated combinations but is licensed only under the proposition's uniform small-shift statement, its localization T<=w<=2T, smoothing scale Delta=T^(1-delta), and mollifier-length restriction; it proves nothing without the proposition's missing main term.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Recognizes the two-shift family as a generating representation and isolates the hypotheses that make derivative extraction meaningful, while separating that explicit analytic step from any unverified claim about preservation of the error term.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because analyticity, Cauchy extraction, localization, and smoothing are explicit enough to support the conceptual compression without formula repair.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span states a proposition uniform in small a,b and w with alpha=a/log T, beta=b/log T, localized w and Delta, and theta<4/7. parents.title: Estermann functional equations and contour residues isolate the mollified mean's diagonal main term

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: At prose level, the main-term extraction has four distinct stages: Estermann-type continuation and functional equations support a Mellin contour transformation; moving the defining contour for g crosses a pole at s=1-alpha whose contribution is declared negligible; the zeta functional equation is applied before the integral is split onto the two rays L_A and L_{-A}, producing J1 and J2 with main, remainder, and error pieces; and a separate local contour calculation near v=1 evaluates the main piece, after which the M1 and M2 sums give the same contribution. This isolates a main term but does not control the remaining off-diagonal errors.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Orders the named analytic transformations by function: dualization makes contour movement possible, the negligible crossed pole is disposed of separately, ray splitting creates symmetric pieces, and the local residue identifies their common main contribution while leaving error control as an independent obligation.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the prose exposes the full transformation sequence and its unresolved error boundary even though formula-level reuse is unsafe.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: Lemmas 4-5 introduce the Estermann-type series, continuation, functional equations, Mellin inversion, and contour motion. Lemma 6 deforms a local path around v=1 and evaluates it by the residue theorem. The proof of Lemma 2 explicitly crosses the s=1-alpha pole, applies the zeta functional equation, splits paths to L_A and L_{-A}, writes J1=M1+R1+E1 with a similar decomposition for J2, and says the summed M2 expression equals the M1 expression.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The dual-series interpretation is a bounded inference. The term is not called diagonal, and exact Estermann functions, kernels, phases, residue factors, interchanges, and uniformity conditions are quarantined because this span is highly scan-dependent.

parents.title: Dyadic decomposition reduces all off-diagonal errors to one averaged Kloosterman bound

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: After the R1 remainder is discarded by rapid decay, the surviving E1 term is represented as a double contour integral whose analytic kernel G is separated from an arithmetic sum J. Extracting g=(h,k) and dyadically boxing N,U,V makes two contour regimes explicit: when UV>=TN the s-path is moved to the eta line and may cross the pole at s=1; when UV<TN it remains on the 1+eta line. Lemmas 7 and 8 then provide independent kernel and arithmetic bounds, with Lemma 8 visibly assuming y<=T^(8/13). Viewing the boxes as an interface between archimedean decay and arithmetic cancellation is inferential; the final 4/7 recovery is formula-dependent in this artifact.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies how the representation routes each size box before estimation and keeps the internal 8/13 hypothesis distinct from the externally reported final mollifier range; the reduction does not itself prove Lemma 8, which is deferred to the next unit.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the decay removal, gcd/dyadic reduction, two-case contour routing, and readable auxiliary hypothesis support a precise mechanism while the damaged exponent conclusion is explicitly withheld.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span bounds R1 as negligible, writes E1 through Z with factors G and J, reorganizes J by gcd and dyadic N,U,V, states the two UV-versus-TN contour choices and the possible s=1 residue, and records Lemmas 7-8 including the y<=T^(8/13) hypothesis. It then combines their bounds, but the concluding exponent display is damaged.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The analytic/arithmetic interface is interpretation. Exact bounds, the residue factor, and the derivation of theta<4/7 are scan-dependent and are not claimed as independently recovered here.

parents.title: A linear differential choice converts surviving sign changes into simple zeta zeros

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: For simple zeros the argument literally subtracts zeros of the full auxiliary function eta from the previously counted zeros of Re eta. With Q restricted to degree one, the remaining events Re eta=0 and eta nonzero are stated to imply xi=0 and xi' nonzero, hence a simple zeta zero. Interpreting eta-nonvanishing as a transversality filter is useful but only analogical: the actual mechanism is the subtraction followed by the specialized implication, and it is unavailable for unrestricted Q.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Distinguishes abundance from certification: Re eta supplies the larger candidate count, subtracting eta-zeros removes failures, and the degree-one relation converts survivors into certified simple zeros while reducing optimization freedom.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the subtraction mechanism and logical consequence are explicit in prose, and the record does not rely on reconstructing the damaged identity.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span says the left side lower-bounds points where Re eta vanishes but eta does not, then states that under the degree-one specialization this gives xi=0 but xi' nonzero and therefore a simple zero. It also explicitly adds the condition that Q have degree one.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The transversality language is marked as interpretation. The exact algebra and normalization of the unreadable identity (42) are quarantined pending scan verification; only its prose-stated implication is retained.

parents.title: The mollified mean square becomes a quadratic functional minimized by an Euler-Lagrange equation

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The mean-value result supplies, for mollifiers in the stated sub-4/7 range, a main term that the source reorganizes as a quadratic functional of the mollifier profile P. With P(0)=0 and P(1)=1, Euler–Lagrange variation yields a linear second-order boundary-value equation. Its optimizer is not itself a polynomial, so the explicit statement that it can be uniformly approximated by polynomials of the required kind is the step that closes the gap between the variational solution and the admissible mollifier family. The degree-one restriction on Q for simple zeros leaves less freedom than the separate choice used for the total critical-line proportion.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the admissibility closure in the optimization: arithmetic analysis first makes a functional available, the ODE solves its relaxed problem, and polynomial approximation returns that solution to the permitted coefficient class. The precise optimum still depends on the damaged mean-value formula.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the variational architecture and polynomial-approximation caveat are explicitly recoverable and yield a concrete mechanism beyond restatement, with formula-level claims withheld.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span states Theorem 2 with theta<4/7, displays a quadratic expression involving P, P', and coefficients A, B, C, gives the Euler–Lagrange ODE and endpoint data, notes uniform approximation of the nonpolynomial solution by suitable polynomials, and reports the 0.4013 and 0.4077 numerical outcomes for distinct Q choices.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Calling the quadratic functional an energy and P's interior a control is an inference. Exact theorem coefficients, weight definitions, functional factors, and numerical reproduction are scan-dependent and are not transcribed from the OCR.
